data.title: Airbnb "back in growth mode" -- analysts
data.description:
Airbnb reported another impressive quarter with gross bookings up 21%, first time bookers growing at the fastest pace in four years, and nights and seats booked outperforming rivals  Expedia and Booking Holdings , all of which beat expectations and impressed investors enough to drive the company’s stock towards the all-time high.

The strength of the quarter led to an upbeat outlook for the current quarter and full year, “running contrary to the more cautious tone from online travel agent (OTA) peers,” notes CFRA analyst Alex Fasciano.

The outlook is supported by evolving travel trends (with travelers more willing to try alternative lodgings), the value proposition compared to hotels, and Airbnb’s investment in technology, the latter of which Needham’s Bernie McTernan sees as one of the “primary drivers of growth.”

“Ai initiatives should continue to drive operating leverage, while the announced agent launch in the first half of 2027 should transform how customers book their overall travel experience,” McTernan adds.

While at the same time, Airbnb’s expanding supply, new features, and AI tools “should support resilience against a softer travel backdrop and strengthen the user experience as AI-agent adoption grows,“ said Bloomberg Intelligence analyst Nicole D’Souza.

These are all multiple product catalysts going forward, and with cost efficiencies associated with greater reliance on AI for customer support, Citi Research analyst Ronald Josey thinks this gives Airbnb the leverage to continue to invest in products while still delivering margin expansion.

Another lever is the benefits of the rent now, pay later (RNPL) option, now eligible on roughly half of all bookings, and which contributed ~3% of net lift to nights booked. Even excluding the impact on RNPL, nights and seats booked growth still accelerated by 13%.

“I think it’s probably pretty obvious that this product makes traveling more affordable…and what we see is that people not only book more, they book earlier, so our lead times have expanded and they book more expensive listings,” Airbnb CFO Ellie Mertz said on the earnings call.

With the company back in growth mode, “the growth trajectory has become more visible, which explains why the stock is outperforming,” an observation noted by Seeking Alpha analyst Luca Socci.

data.title: European Stocks Tumble On AI Regulation Fears
data.description:
BRUSSELS/FRANKFURT/PARIS (dpa-AFX) - European stocks tumbled on Friday as risk appetite fell amid rising fears of tighter AI regulations by the Trump administration. Investors also reacted to corporate earnings announcements and the latest batch of regional and U.S. economic data.

Uncertainty about the potential economic impact of the Democrats' sweeping win in the US midterm elections contributed to the reduced risk appetite in global markets.

It is feared that Democratic Party's sweeping wins in the US midterm elections could result in tighter regulation of the AI industry and slowdown in data center expansion.

The pan European Stoxx 600 ended down 1.84%. The UK's FTSE 100, Germany's DAX and France's CAC 40 settled lower by 2.21%, 2.33% and 1.83%, respectively. Switzerland's SMI closed 1.14% down.

Among other markets in Europe, Austria, Belgium, Czech Republic, Denmark, Finland, Greece, Ireland, Italy, Netherlands, Norway, Poland, Spain and Sweden closed weak.

Iceland and Türkiye ended higher, while Portugal and Russia closed flat.

In the UK market, BT Group tumbled 6%. Metlen Energy & Metals dropped nearly 5%, while Airtel Africa, The Sage Group, Hiscox, Admiral Group, Next, British American Tobacco, Imperial Brands, Associated British Foods, National Grid, Marks & Spencer, Ithaca Energy, Unilever and Experian lost 2%-4%.

Coca-Cola HBC climbed more than 3%. Scottish Mortgage gained 2.2%, while Endeavour Mining, IAG, Rolls Royce Holdings and Intercontinental Hotels moved up 1%-1.7%.

In the German market, Deutsche Post, Hannover RE, Munich RE, Siemens, Rheinmetall, BMW, Allianz, BASF, Deutsche Bank, Brenntag, Mercedes-Benz and Zalando ended down 3%-5%.

Daimler Truck Holding drifted lower by 3.7% despite a 73% jump in Q3 adjusted operating profit and reaffirmed full-year guidance, as nine-month results remained below year-ago levels.

Adidas, SAP, Volkswagen, Deutsche Boerse, Bayer, Symrise, Commerzbank, E.ON, Beiersdorf, Hochtief and Deutsche Telekom also ended notably lower.

Siemens Energy climbed 4%. RWE and Fresenius posted moderate gains.

In the French market, Teleperformance tanked 15% after the company cut its 2026 revenue outlook.

Capgemini, LVMH, Hermes International, Kering, Danone, AXA and Bouygues closed lower by 2%-3%.

Publicis Groupe, Edenred, Orange, Dassault Systemes, L'Oreal, TotalEnergies, Vinci, Pernod Ricard and Sanofi also ended weak.

STMicroelectronics, Legrand, EssilorLuxottica and Stellantis gained 1%-1.7%.

In economic news, UK house prices declined for the third straight month in October, marking their quickest in three years. House prices dropped 1.2% on an annual basis in October, faster than the 0.1% slight decrease in September. Weaker housing demand was due to renewed inflationary pressures, driven in part by the conflict in the Middle East. On a monthly basis, house prices dropped 0.6%.

France's trade deficit widened to €7.3 billion in September from a revised €6.0 billion in August, well above expectations of €5.8 billion. Imports rose 4.0% month-on-month to €62.7 billion, while exports rose at a softer 2.0% to €55.3 billion.

Germany's industrial production expanded for the second straight month in September amid significant output growth in the automotive industry, official data showed.

Industrial output expanded 0.7% on a monthly basis, slower than the revised 1% rebound in August, Destatis said. Meanwhile, economists had expected a flat change.

On a yearly basis, industrial production rose 0.4% in September, slower than the 0.7% increase in the prior month.

data.title: Private equity-owned landlord to pay $49.8 million over hidden fees
data.description:
By Jody Godoy

Progress Residential, the biggest US manager of single family rental homes, will pay $49.8 million to settle allegations by the Federal Trade Commission and four states that it deceived renters with hidden fees, an FTC official told Reuters on Friday.

The action builds on the FTC's work tackling corporate cost of living issues, as it explores requiring landlords to list mandatory fees and charges upfront as part of advertised rental rates.

Progress violated the law with charges, such as smart home fees or fees for lack of renters' insurance, that were not included in advertised rental rates, the FTC official said.

Roughly 35% of Americans rent their homes. According to a survey by Zillow, 60% of renters paid a recurring fee on top of rent last year.

Progress also routinely failed to return renters' security deposits and advertised homes as "move-in ready" that were in need of serious cleaning or repairs, the official said.

The FTC is receiving $48.5 million, which it will use to reimburse harmed consumers, and Arizona is receiving $1.25 million, the official said. Colorado, Indiana, and Utah were also expected to join the settlement.

Progress is a subsidiary of Pretium, a real-estate focused investment firm that owns and manages more than 82,000 rental homes across the US.

The company founded by former Goldman Sachs executive Don Mullen has said it aims to become one of the biggest homebuilding lenders by 2027.

Invitation Homes , another owner of single family rental homes launched in the wake of the subprime mortgage crisis, agreed to pay $48 million to settle an FTC action over hidden fees in 2024.

data.title: AI Stocks Rebound After Brutal Week for Nasdaq — WSJ
data.description:
The AI trade has for now stopped spiraling, after a bruising selloff that set back the Nasdaq by about $2.5 trillion yesterday.

The tech-heavy index is gaining more than 1%, reversing some of Thursday's historic losses. The Dow, on the other hand, is about flat on the day after paring morning losses.

The stocks that were hardest-hit this week, including data-center firms like CoreWeave and chip companies Intel, Nvidia, Micron and ARM Holdings, are all climbing.

Meanwhile, this morning's jobs report pointed to robust hiring in October. The economy added 165,000 jobs and the unemployment rate slipped to 4.1%, beating economists' expectations.

Global stocks swooned overnight, as tech-heavy indexes in Asia caught up with yesterday's losses in the U.S. SoftBank, one of OpenAI's biggest investors, slid 10% in Tokyo.

The losses came as sentiment toward the AI trade had already grown more fragile. After Democrats' sweeping midterm victory, the question now is whether this week's selloff was a temporary stumble, or the start of a longer-lasting unwinding of the AI trade.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).

Raymond, PTC Industries, Rossel Techsys, and Axiscades are some of the key small aerospace and defence companies with promising growth prospects. Experts decode their outlook and technical targets.

Raymond Limited recently got approval from board to be renamed as Raymond Aerospace, Defence & Engineering Limited (subject to further regulatory approvals). Its order book supports a long runway, but it is not a one-year executable backlog, and RFQs are not firm orders, highlighted Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research, Ventura.

Raymond share price closed 4.32% lower at Rs.1082 per share on BSE with a market capitalisation of Rs.7,220.24 crore on Friday. The stock has delivered 154% return in 2026 so far and 92% return in one year.

They can maintain a stop loss of Rs.995 per share and target for Rs.1,140.00 / Rs.1,198.50) or on a breakout close above Rs.1,135.00 (SL: Rs.1,080.00, Targets: Rs.1,198.50 / Rs.1,280.00). data.title: Chandra hire D'Souza is Voltas chair; Trent MD joins board
data.description:
Bengaluru and Mumbai, Nov. 6 -- Voltas Ltd on Friday named Tata Consumer Products chief executive officer Sunil D'Souza as its next chairman, replacing Noel Tata, who is stepping down going by the Tata Group's retirement rules for non-executive directors.

The appointment puts one of Noel's longest-held board positions in the hands of an executive hired by Tata Sons chairman N. Chandrasekaran, who chairs Tata Consumer, and is Noel's rival in a deepening leadership tussle within the group.

D'Souza, who joined the Voltas board only in May, will take charge on 12 November, a day after Noel retires. He had earned his spurs by turning around Whirlpool's Indian subsidiary.

Noel, who had joined the Voltas board in 2003, has been appointed chairman emeritus, with the board acknowledging his "distinguished leadership" and "unwavering commitment" to the company's progress.

The Voltas board has also appointed Venkatesalu Palaniswamy as an additional director in a non-executive capacity. Palaniswamy is the managing director of Trent Ltd, and has worked alongside Noel Tata to build scale at the apparel retailer.

The top-deck changes at Voltas come barely a week after Trent named longtime Noel ally Bahram Vakil as its next chairman. Two executives familiar with the matter told Mint that the appointment was made without keeping Chandrasekaran in the loop.

The appointments at Trent and Voltas offer a different picture of how the battle for influence is playing out across Tata companies. For now, the Trent leadership appears to have favoured Noel's choice, while the Voltas appointments appear to have come through consensus, stressing continuity in the management, according an executive privy to the development.

In other developments at Voltas, Mukundan Menon C.P., the current managing director of Voltas, will also retire on 24 May 2027, after a short tenure. Mukundan, hired from Blue Star last year and seen as a 'bridge MD', will be replaced by Jayant Balan, a Voltas veteran who leads the company's room air-conditioner business.

Balan will take over on 25 May for five years, subject to shareholder approval. Balan joined the Tata Group through the Tata Administrative Service in 1999 and moved to Voltas in 2001.

Earlier this year, Noel decided to leave the boards of five public Tata companies and one privately owned firm. On Thursday, he stepped down as vice-chairman of Titan Co Ltd, which has not yet named a replacement.

Tata Steel Ltd's board meets on Saturday, followed by Tata Investment Corp Ltd. Tata International Ltd, the group's $3.6 billion private trading business, is the sixth company he is expected to leave next week.

Each change is seen as a sign of the growing conflict between Noel and Chandrasekaran, who has the backing of the Tata Sons board, including Venu Srinivasan, the other Tata Trusts nominee on the board.

Noel's choice to follow the group's governance rules also raises questions about Tata Sons' decision to let Chandrasekaran stay beyond the retirement age: the Group has set retirement at 65 for executive directors, and Chandrasekaran would be 69 by the time he finishes his third five-year term in 2032.

Tata Trusts' nominees on the board of Tata Sons do not have a retirement age and for this reason, both Noel, who turns 70, and Srinivasan, who will be 74 next month, can continue.

data.title: Flash Heard: Texas Power Giant Says Blue Wave Doesn't Spell Doom for Data Centers — WSJ
data.description:
By Jinjoo Lee

What does the blue wave mean for Texas power plant owners?

Vistra, the largest electricity generator in Texas, suffered the worst stock price plunge among its power plant operator peers since Tuesday, with shares falling 19% through Thursday. Friday's 10% rally only partially reversed that decline.

The state, a hotbed of data-center activity, elected Democratic governor Gina Hinojosa. Democrats won a majority in the Texas House of Representatives, too, though Republicans retained their majority in the Texas Senate.

Vistra doesn't think the blue wave spells doom for data-center development. Asked about a prolonged moratorium on data centers in Texas on its Friday earnings call, Vistra Chief Executive Officer Jim Burke said that is a "bridge too far from where the dialogue is at this point," based on conversations the company is having with legislators.

"I have not heard the governor-elect and I haven't heard the legislature say that they do not want Texas to have any of this [data center] load." What is more likely is higher standards around which data centers get to connect to the grid, he said.

Wholesale forward power prices in Texas have already been going the wrong way for power plant owners, declining more than 20% year to date, according to a report from Jefferies. Part of that can be blamed on the data center permitting pause that current Republican Gov. Greg Abbott put in place.

Even after Friday's uptick, Vistra's forward earnings multiple of 12.6 times is about 44% lower than where it was a year earlier. Its valuation might stay pressured until Texas' newly elected politicians give clarity on their long-term data center policies.

This item is part of a Wall Street Journal live coverage event. The full stream can be found by searching P/WSJL (WSJ Live Coverage).
